elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall ...", so every covered ending (natural expiry, non-renewal and any termination) triggers the obligations, and the 30-day return runs "within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination" — not from a request or from anticipated expiry only.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "provide the Company with transition assistance for up to six (6) months". The obligation is unconditional (no request precondition), and the six-month ceiling matches the preferred position.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) ends "at HDI's then-current rates" — the pricing basis is expressly the vendor's then-current rates, as the preferred position requires.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, return to the Company all Content, user information and other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company". The temporal anchor is expiry/termination itself (not a request), and the data scope covers all categories belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company rather than selected named types.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return "in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after such return, delete such Content, user information and data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to the Company" — deletion is expressly sequenced after return and is accompanied by written certification, avoiding the walk-away risk of immediate deletion on termination.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same trigger language: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "transition assistance for up to six (6) months" makes at least 90 days of assistance available, exceeding the fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Company data in a standard machine-readable format within thirty (30) days after expiry or termination.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements appear in the single inserted paragraph in operative language, with correct temporal anchors (30 days running from expiry/termination, not from a request) and correct sequencing (certified deletion only after return).

The finding is correctly classified as missing: Section 4.1 addresses only term and notice, 4.1(c) only the Termination Payment, and 10.7 preserves Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 — no existing exit, data-return or deletion mechanic exists in a hosting agreement where HDI holds the Company's Content, user information and order data.

Minimal: the redline is a single concise insertion in the termination section and changes no other word of the Agreement. Nothing favourable to the Company is deleted, no duplicate operative term is created, and no extras (survival tail, at-own-expense wording, added damages categories, procedures or boilerplate) are bolted on. The drafter also dropped the model language's "at Customer's request" precondition, which is more favourable to us and does not add any requirement outside the checklist.

Intent preserved: the Termination Payment instalment mechanic in 4.1(c), the 90-day notice/auto-renewal structure in 4.1 and the two-year survival window in 10.7 all survive without contradiction; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is introduced (the data scope is described descriptively — "Content, user information and other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company" — rather than by reference to an undefined "Customer Data" term).

Non-blocking drafting notes for the drafter (not defects requiring repair): (i) the rendered insertion carries the heading "Transition Assistance; Return of Data." but no section number, while the margin comment calls it "Section 4.3" — number the clause 4.3 on execution so the comment and the document align; (ii) Section 10.7 lists only Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 as surviving. The new clause is self-executing on expiry/termination so it operates on its own terms, and adding a survival tail would be a non-minimal extra, but if HDI argues 10.7 is exhaustive we can add "4.3" to the 10.7 list as a second-round tidy.
